concept.name: Tweezer top
concept.definition: A pattern of two or more candlesticks whose highs match (or nearly match), forming an even 'tweezer' line at a price ceiling, typically appearing in an uptrend. Technical analysts read the repeated rejection of the same high as a minor bearish reversal signal, which gains weight when the candles themselves form other reversal shapes.
concept.intuition: The market probed the exact same ceiling twice and failed both times, as if pinched by tweezers at that price, suggesting sellers are defending that level.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: two or more candles (consecutive or separated) share essentially equal highs; the first is typically a white candle and the second a black candle in the classic uptrend form. The matching highs define an ad-hoc resistance level whose subsequent break invalidates the bearish reading.
concept.failure_modes: Matching highs occur constantly by chance, so isolated tweezer tops have low standalone significance. In strong uptrends the double test often precedes a breakout rather than a reversal.
concept.misconceptions: The candles do not have to be adjacent, and their bodies can be any size; what matters is the matching highs. It is a minor signal on its own, not a major reversal pattern like an evening star.
concept.example: A stock rallies and prints a white candle with a high of 77.00, then the next session trades up to 77.00 again but closes lower as a black candle. The tweezer top marks 77.00 as resistance and warns of a possible pullback.
